project_info.brief_explanation: Technical setup guide for a football match management application featuring a Node.js backend and a React-based frontend.
project_info.source_context: Local development and testing setup instructions.

sections.title: Quick Start Guide: Football Match Manager
sections.raw_content: This guide provides instructions for setting up and running the Football Match Manager application locally for development and testing purposes.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.raw_content:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed on your machine:

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (v18 or later)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) (comes with Node.js) or [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/)
- [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) (v14 or later)
- [Git](https://git-scm.com/)

sections.title: 1. Clone the Repository
sections.raw_content:
```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd football-match-manager
```

sections.title: Backend
sections.raw_content:
```bash
cd backend
npm install
```

sections.title: Frontend
sections.raw_content:
```bash
cd ../frontend
npm install
```

sections.title: 3. Set Up the Database
4. Configure Environment Variables
sections.raw_content:
Create a `.env` file in the `backend` directory based on the provided `.env.example`:

```bash
cd backend
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit the `.env` file to match your database configuration:

```
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=football_match_manager
DB_USER=your_username
DB_PASSWORD=your_password

sections.title: JWT secret for authentication (use a strong, random string in production)
sections.raw_content: JWT_SECRET=your_super_secret_jwt_key_change_in_production

sections.title: Port for the backend server
sections.raw_content: PORT=5000

sections.title: Optional: Third-party football API key (if required by the chosen API)
sections.raw_content:
FOOTBALL_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

sections.title: 5. Run Database Migrations
sections.raw_content:
We use Sequelize for ORM and migrations. Run the following to set up the database schema:

```bash
npx sequelize-cli db:migrate
```

sections.title: 6. Seed Initial Data (Optional)
sections.raw_content:
If you have seed data for leagues, teams, etc., you can run:

```bash
npx sequelize-cli db:seed:all
```

sections.title: Backend
sections.raw_content: ```bash

sections.title: From the backend directory
sections.raw_content:
npm run dev
```
The backend server will start on `http://localhost:5000` (or the port specified in your .env file).

sections.title: Frontend
sections.raw_content: ```bash

sections.title: From the frontend directory (in a new terminal)
sections.raw_content:
npm start
```
The frontend development server will start on `http://localhost:3000`.

sections.title: 8. Verify the Setup
sections.raw_content: Open your browser and navigate to `http://localhost:3000`. You should see the Football Match Manager home page.

sections.title: Backend (`backend` directory)
sections.raw_content:
- `npm run dev`: Start the server in development mode with auto-restart
- `npm start`: Start the server in production mode
- `npm test`: Run the test suite
- `npm run lint`: Run ESLint for code quality

sections.title: Frontend (`frontend` directory)
sections.raw_content:
- `npm start`: Start the development server
- `npm run build`: Build the production bundle
- `npm test`: Run the test suite
- `npm run eject`: Eject from Create React App (use with caution)

sections.title: Backend Tests
sections.raw_content: ```bash

sections.title: From the backend directory
sections.raw_content:
npm test
```

sections.title: Frontend Tests
sections.raw_content: ```bash

sections.title: From the frontend directory
sections.raw_content:
npm test
```

sections.title: API Documentation
sections.raw_content:
Once the backend is running, you can view the API documentation at:
`http://localhost:5000/api-docs` (if Swagger/OpenAPI documentation is enabled)

sections.title: Common Issues
sections.raw_content:
1. **Database Connection Errors**
   - Verify that PostgreSQL is running
   - Check your `.env` file for correct database credentials
   - Ensure the database exists and the user has sufficient privileges

2. **Port Already in Use**
   - Another process is using the port specified in your `.env` file
   - Either change the port or stop the conflicting process

3. **Module Not Found Errors**
   - Ensure you have run `npm install` in both `backend` and `frontend` directories
   - Try deleting `node_modules` and `package-lock.json` (or `yarn.lock`) and reinstalling

4. **Authentication Issues**
   - Verify that the JWT secret is set correctly in the `.env` file
   - Ensure you are sending the token in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`

sections.title: Next Steps
sections.raw_content:
After getting the application running locally, you can:

1. Explore the API endpoints using tools like Postman or curl
2. Begin implementing features based on the specification
3. Write additional tests to improve coverage
4. Prepare for deployment by setting up production environments

sections.title: Support
sections.raw_content: If you encounter any issues or have questions, please refer to the project documentation or contact the development team.

elements.content: Node.js v18 or later is required.
PostgreSQL v14 or later is required.
Database named 'football_match_manager' for application data storage.
Authentication must be handled via JWT using a strong secret key and Bearer token in the Authorization header.
The application must use Sequelize for ORM and database migrations.
The application is successfully running when the home page is accessible at http://localhost:3000.
API documentation should be available via Swagger/OpenAPI at /api-docs.

structural_gaps.remediation_advice: The document is a setup guide. A business-oriented document defining the purpose and goals of the Football Match Manager is needed.
No business rules or user features (e.g., match creation, team management) are defined. A functional spec is required.
Define the boundaries of the application to avoid scope creep.
